statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-108472: xfs_admin in xfsprogs builds the argument strings for xfs_db, xfs_repair and xfs_io and runs them through eval, so a crafted label, UUID or device argument can run shell commands, which becomes local privilege escalation where xfs_admin runs as root, for example from udisks (https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/11/11/27). The upstream fix removes eval and passes every argument through the positional parameters (https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/fs/xfs/xfsprogs-dev.git/commit/?id=1c122bbd3c88d89695d3b60c1070d87073d56121). This owner publishes two builds for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine repository, 7.0.1-r0 and 7.0.1-r1, both builds of xfsprogs 7.0.1; xfs_admin ships in the xfsprogs-extra package as /usr/sbin/xfs_admin. We checked xfsprogs-extra of both builds on x86_64 and aarch64 against the index checksum. In 7.0.1-r0 xfs_admin still runs xfs_io, xfs_db and xfs_repair through eval with the option strings unquoted. In 7.0.1-r1 xfs_admin carries the upstream fix, backported to 7.0.1: it collects the options as flags, passes them with set --, and no longer calls eval (the word appears only in a comment). The range ends at 7.0.1-r1, the first build with the fix.
